content: 1. Female patients or female partners of male patients should avoid pregnancy while undergoing combination therapy with PEG-IFN-alpha-2a and ribavirin. This is due to the significant teratogenic and/or embryocidal effects demonstrated in all animal species exposed to ribavirin. 2. Life-threatening or fatal neuropsychiatric reactions, including suicide, suicidal ideation, homicidal ideation, depression, relapse of drug addiction, and drug overdose, may occur during treatment. These reactions can manifest regardless of a prior history of psychiatric illness. 3. Cardiovascular complications such as hypertension, supraventricular arrhythmias, chest pain, and myocardial infarction have been reported. Patients with pre-existing cardiovascular disease should be treated with caution. 4. Bone marrow suppression may occur, potentially leading to severe cytopenias. Ribavirin can exacerbate neutropenia and lymphopenia caused by alpha interferons. Rare cases of aplastic anemia have also been observed. 5. Autoimmune disorders, including myositis, hepatitis, thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura, psoriasis, rheumatoid arthritis, interstitial nephritis, thyroiditis, and systemic lupus erythematosus, may develop or worsen during treatment. 6. Endocrine disorders such as hypothyroidism, hyperthyroidism, hyperglycemia, hypoglycemia, and diabetes mellitus may be caused or exacerbated by this therapy. 7. Alpha interferons may induce or worsen ophthalmic disorders, including decreased or lost vision, retinopathy (e.g., macular edema, retinal artery or vein thrombosis, retinal hemorrhages, and cotton wool spots), optic neuritis, papilledema, and serous retinal detachment. 8. Patients with chronic hepatitis C (CHC) and cirrhosis are at risk of hepatic decompensation and death when treated with alpha interferons. 9. Exacerbations of hepatitis during hepatitis B therapy are not uncommon and are characterized by transient and potentially severe increases in serum ALT levels. 10. Pulmonary complications, including dyspnea, pulmonary infiltrates, pneumonia, bronchiolitis obliterans, interstitial pneumonitis, pulmonary hypertension, and sarcoidosis, have been reported. Some cases have resulted in respiratory failure and/or death. 11. Serious and severe infections (bacterial, viral, or fungal), some of which have been fatal, have been reported during treatment with alpha interferons. 12. Ulcerative and hemorrhagic/ischemic colitis, sometimes fatal, has been observed within 12 weeks of starting alpha interferon treatment. 13. Pancreatitis, including fatal cases, has occurred during combination therapy with alpha interferon and ribavirin. 14. Severe acute hypersensitivity reactions, such as urticaria, angioedema, bronchoconstriction, and anaphylaxis, have been reported. 15. Growth inhibition has been observed in children aged 5–17 years with CHC during combination therapy with ribavirin for up to 48 weeks, as well as in children aged 3–17 years with chronic hepatitis B (CHB) during monotherapy. 16. There are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women to determine drug-associated risks. Combination therapy with ribavirin is contraindicated in pregnant women and in the male partners of pregnant women. 17. There is no information regarding the presence of this drug in human milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its effects on milk production. HIV-infected mothers are advised not to breastfeed to avoid potential HIV transmission. Therefore, CHCand CHB-infected mothers co-infected with HIV should not breastfeed. 18. Peginterferon alfa-2a is an immunomodulatory cytokine that enhances the phagocytic activity of macrophages and the cytotoxic activity of lymphocytes against target cells. It is administered subcutaneously, typically in the abdomen or thigh, avoiding the navel and waistline. 19. The solution should be visually inspected before use. It should appear clear and colorless to slightly yellowish, without particulates. If particulates or discoloration are present, the product should be discarded. 20. Common side effects include flu-like symptoms (e.g., headache, fatigue, fever, chills, and muscle aches), nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, dry mouth, loss of appetite, dizziness, trouble sleeping, and redness/swelling at the injection site. These symptoms usually decrease after the first few weeks of treatment. 21. To reduce flu-like symptoms, the medication can be injected at bedtime, and fever reducers/pain relievers like acetaminophen can be used before each dose. 22. Dry mouth may worsen dental issues. Patients should drink plenty of water, use saliva substitutes, brush their teeth at least twice daily, and have regular dental exams. 23. Temporary hair loss may occur during treatment. 24. This medication may cause serious mental or mood changes, including severe depression and suicidal thoughts or attempts, which may worsen during or after treatment. 25. Peginterferon alfa-2a may lower the body’s ability to fight infections, increasing the risk of serious or fatal infections or worsening existing infections. 26. Patients should avoid contact with individuals who have contagious infections (e.g., chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, flu) and inform healthcare professionals about their use of this medication before receiving any vaccinations. 27. This drug may cause dizziness. Alcohol or marijuana use can exacerbate this effect. Patients should avoid driving or operating machinery until they are sure they can do so safely. 28. Children may be more sensitive to the mental/mood side effects of this drug, and their growth may be slowed, potentially resulting in a lower final adult height. 29. Pregnant women or those planning to become pregnant should not use this medication, as it may harm an unborn baby. Reliable birth control methods should be used during treatment. 30. Patients should store the medication in the refrigerator, away from light and moisture, and should not freeze it. It should not be left out of the refrigerator for more than 24 hours. Expired or unused medication should be properly discarded. 31. Patients should not change brands of interferon without consulting their doctor or pharmacist. 32. If a dose is missed, it should be used as soon as remembered, provided it is within two days of the scheduled dose. The next dose should be taken on the usual day. 33. Regular lab tests (e.g., blood counts, thyroid tests, virus levels, kidney/liver function, triglyceride levels, eye exams) should be conducted before and during treatment to monitor the patient’s condition and response to therapy.
